title: When Dense Optical Flow Measures the Background Instead of the Hand: Silent Object Switching Under Egocentric Camera Motion
description: Box-median dense optical flow inside a detected hand box under egocentric camera motion silently switches from tracking the hand to tracking the background. On rendered two-plane scenes under a calibrated fisheye lens (hand at 0.45 m, background at 2.5 m, depth ratio 0.18), OpenCV Farneback at 960x540 crosses half gain at 28.2 px (sd 2.7 over 20 texture seeds; 29.4 px on a nine-point grid) and settles on a shelf at 0.19 (sd 0.01), equal to the depth ratio. Three distinct estimators—OpenCV DIS (42.2 px, shelf 0.19), RAFT-small (40.4 px, shelf 0.18), and five-times-larger RAFT-large (40.0 px, shelf 0.18)—shift the crossing and land on the same geometric shelf, while all 6,213 seeded measurements across every sweep return finite, non-null fields. Direct pixel-level inspection at 68.0 px confirms the mechanism: 89.4% to 98.0% of inside-box pixels lie closer to background flow than hand flow (RAFT-large locks onto the background to within 0.1 px median endpoint error), collapsing the pipeline's ego-motion-subtracted residual to 6.5%-21.1% of true relative speed. A matched static-camera, moving-hand control eliminates the 0.18 shelf (post-68.0 px gain falls to 0.0002-0.092) and shifts every estimator's crossing earlier by 3%-23%, showing that the shelf is an ego-motion property and the crossing is governed by the velocity discontinuity across the hand-box boundary. Controlled multi-seed sweeps confirm that the shelf tracks the depth ratio across 0.10 to 0.50, that larger boxes delay collapse for RAFT-small (20.1 to 108.7 px) while Farneback saturates (19.3 to 34.5 px), that additive Gaussian noise degrades low-displacement gain and shifts crossings earlier, and that horizontal motion blur trades fine-scale accuracy for reduced spatial aliasing. Under the wide-angle lens alone, scalar-median ego-motion subtraction leaves a rotational residual 76x larger than on a narrow lens, exhausting a 0.25 HAL (4.4% speed) error budget at 26.5 deg/s of head rotation or 3.1 cm/s of translation. This study is synthetic, with no corpus exposure measurement or expert ergonomic validation; it isolates a reproducible, silent failure mode of egocentric box-median flow pipelines. Not peer reviewed. Code and data: https://github.com/caiotheodoro/cyclegraph
